overview: Once a breadboard circuit is working and needs to survive being moved, bumped, or left running unattended, it usually gets rebuilt on perfboard — a rigid board with the same 0.1-inch hole grid as a breadboard, but meant for soldering rather than plugging in. Plain perfboard has isolated copper pads at each hole (every connection needs a wire or solder bridge); stripboard instead has continuous copper strips running the length of the board, which speeds up circuits that need several components in a row but requires cutting the strip wherever two points on the same strip need to be electrically separate.
simpleSummary: A solderable board with the same hole layout as a breadboard, for making a working circuit permanent.

specifications.holeSpacing: 0.1 inch (2.54mm), matching breadboard and standard header pin spacing
specifications.perfboardType: Isolated copper pad per hole — every connection needs a wire or solder joint
specifications.stripboardType: Continuous copper strips along one axis — faster for in-line connections, needs strip-cutting for isolation
specifications.material: Fiberglass (FR4) or phenolic resin substrate with copper cladding

pinMap.name: Pad/Strip
pinMap.function: An individual copper contact point (perfboard) or a segment of a continuous copper strip (stripboard) where component leads are soldered.
pinMap.currentLimit: Depends on copper trace width/thickness — thin traces limit current more than a breadboard's spring clips would suggest
pinMap.gotcha: On stripboard, forgetting to cut a strip where two things need to be electrically separate is one of the most common 'why is this shorted' debugging sessions in DIY electronics.

pinMap.name: Mounting Hole
pinMap.function: Corner holes (on boards that include them) for physically mounting the board into an enclosure.

useCases.title: Permanent version of a breadboard prototype
useCases.scenario: Rebuild a working breadboard circuit into a soldered, vibration-resistant form for actual use.

useCases.title: Small custom shield/hat
useCases.scenario: Build a simple custom add-on board for a microcontroller when a full PCB isn't justified.

oftenConfusedWith: Breadboard (solderless, temporary, not a permanent solution)
oftenUpgradedTo: Custom-designed PCB for a production-quality, more compact, and more reliable final product
